anatomy_measured.experts: 64 routed + 2 shared, 6 routed active per token
anatomy_measured.why_this_matters: this is the workhorse property. Eight of sixty-six experts run per token, so the compute is ~1.8B while the residency is 30.6 GiB. On a 96 GiB box beside an 11.5 GiB resident that fits with room to spare, and it is the reason an A3B body can be fast without being small.

BANDWIDTH_MEASURED_AND_A_WITHDRAWN_CLAIM.what_that_implied: 30.6 GiB would take ~32 minutes and would explain the GPU timeout, the Falcon 2-hour ETA, and every slow load today
BANDWIDTH_MEASURED_AND_A_WITHDRAWN_CLAIM.WITHDRAWN: that dd was competing with the in-flight 30 GiB Kimi load on the same device. Re-measured with nothing else reading: 822 MB/s.
BANDWIDTH_MEASURED_AND_A_WITHDRAWN_CLAIM.conclusion: the external volume is NOT the bottleneck -- 30.6 GiB at 822 MB/s is about 38 seconds of reads. Moving the workhorse to internal storage is still worth ~3.4x on cold reads, but it is an optimisation, not the fix. The GPU timeout has another cause.
BANDWIDTH_MEASURED_AND_A_WITHDRAWN_CLAIM.lesson: a bandwidth number taken while a multi-gigabyte load is in flight measures the contention, not the device. Third hypothesis withdrawn today by re-measuring rather than reasoning.

SEARCH_HAWKING_FIRST_RESULT.instruction: S007 order 5: search Hawking for existing Kimi/DeepSeek/MLA support before building

FOUND \u2014 architecture recognition is.evidence: run against Kimi's 5679 real tensor names it classifies 99.1% of them: 4992 moe_expert, 328 vision_encoder, 135 latent_attention, 78 shared_expert, 26 moe_router, 53 unrecognised.
FOUND \u2014 architecture recognition is.MLA is a first-class concept there: FINGERPRINTS carries ('latent_attention', r'(kv_a_proj|kv_b_proj|q_a_proj|q_b_proj|kv_a_layernorm)', '*') and it performed the MLA FOLD on Kimi -- recognising that the residual q/o projections belong to the latent-attention organ rather than a second independent GQA organ, and recording why.
FOUND \u2014 architecture recognition is.CONSEQUENCE: do NOT build an MLA projection primitive. S007 warned against a one-model hack when the missing concept is MLA topology; the measurement says the missing thing is not the concept at all. Hawking understands this architecture. What it lacks is an EXECUTION path for it.

SEARCH_HAWKING_FIRST_RESULT.the_organs_are_DECLARED_UNMEASURED: every Kimi organ comes back DECLARED_UNMEASURED -- declared in Hawking's organ registry and never actually measured. That is a real gap this campaign closes, and it is why Kimi is worth the budget.

K1_RESULT.verdict: KIMI EXECUTES. The base organism runs.
K1_RESULT.what_fixed_it: converting offline to an MLX-native 8-bit artifact. The Metal GPU timeout was the ON-LOAD bf16 conversion building one oversized command buffer -- which was the first hypothesis on S007's list, and it is now confirmed by the fix rather than by argument.
K1_RESULT.BYTE_ACCOUNTING_NOTE: the converter reports 8.706 bits per weight for an '8-bit' quantisation. That is the complete rate including scales and zeros, and it is the BitNet lesson again in a new place: a headline precision is not a system rate. Recorded at 8.706, never as 8.

K6_FIRST_TPS.runs: 3 timed runs of 121 completion tokens each, after a discarded warm-up that absorbs kernel compilation
K6_FIRST_TPS.WHAT_THIS_IS_NOT: NOT a like-for-like beat of the 51.6 TPS on record. That figure was measured on a different representation; this is the 8-bit converted body. And the prompt is trivial -- 'count from 1 to 60' -- which is low-entropy generation with a 22-token prompt. Real HCLI work has long prompts and harder content.
K6_FIRST_TPS.hygiene_S004: sealed-3.14 was resident throughout at 11.58 GiB and IDLE (1.2-1.6% CPU) before and after, recorded by gpu_attribution.py. Two foreign servers held nothing. This is NOT a quiesced single-process measurement and is not reported as one.
K6_FIRST_TPS.band: above the ~70 'strong workhorse' band. Per S007 that means stop chasing TPS and go verify capability, which is what happened next.

K2_CAPABILITY_FIRST_RESULT.verdict: FAST AND NOT YET QUALIFIED. 1 of 4 on the calibration set.
K2_CAPABILITY_FIRST_RESULT.kimi_answers: DENSE_DECODER for Dream-v0, iLLaDA and ModernBERT alike; passed only BitNet
K2_CAPABILITY_FIRST_RESULT.INSTRUMENT_VERIFIED_BEFORE_BLAMING_THE_B: the prompt was dumped and checked. It DOES show `config keys of note: {'mask_token_id': 151666}` and it DOES state the rule 'a config exposing mask_token_id, or an architecture ending ForMaskedLM, is NOT autoregressive'. Kimi had the evidence and the rule in front of it and still answered DENSE_DECODER. The failure is the body's, not the harness's.
K2_CAPABILITY_FIRST_RESULT.THE_CORRECTION_IS_MINE: I chose the wrong task for a workhorse. S007's own list for Kimi is mechanical -- bounded WorkUnits, tests, reproduction, inspection, ordinary debugging, ModelLake FIRST-PASS work, Doctor probes, receipt generation, straightforward repairs. Open-vocabulary architecture classification is on none of it. It is judgement-heavy and knowledge-bound, and four bodies across three prompt designs have now failed it. Narrowing the vocabulary did not help; it converted 'wrong words' into 'wrong choice'.
K2_CAPABILITY_FIRST_RESULT.next: redesign the WorkUnit around what the steer actually asked for: work whose answer is CHECKABLE FROM THE MACHINE rather than recalled from pretraining. Running a test and reporting the returncode is that shape. Classifying a diffusion LM is not.
